original_metadata.title: In characteristic zero, the constants of the free-associative derivation Delta(X)=0 and Delta(Y)=X^m for m>=2 have the explicit permissible-bracket free generating set of Theorem 4.6
original_metadata.author: Vesselin Drensky; Leonid Makar-Limanov
original_metadata.source_title: Locally Nilpotent Derivations of Free Algebra of Rank Two
original_metadata.difficulty_reason: The kernel is infinitely generated, so triangularity of the derivation does not identify either its generators or all possible relations. The author proves a weighted spanning theorem using a noncommutative bracket operation and then reconstructs permissible bracket words from leading monomials. The resulting normal-form and indecomposability argument gives an explicit free basis, going beyond a direct application of freeness for a homogeneous kernel.

proof_review.method: Published author proof/core and local context fidelity screening
proof_review.note: The complete Theorem4.6 proof, the kernel-spanning induction4.2/Corollary4.3 and the permissible-word construction4.5 were read. The author first controls every element killed by a power of the derivation using weighted induction and explicit commutators of the bracket operation, then proves kernel generation by permissible bracketed words. The final proof reconstructs each word root and matching brackets uniquely from its leading monomial and rules out a factorization by lower-weight permissible leading words. Select the explicit homogeneous monomial-derivation kernel for m>=2; the short equal-kernel rigidity theorem3.3 and the known linear Weitzenboeck case are not counted.

original_metadata.statement_scope: Exactly the explicit homogeneous case of Theorem4.6 for a field K of characteristic zero and integer m>=2. Work in the free unitary associative algebra K<X,Y> with Delta(X)=0, Delta(Y)=X^m and T_1=YX-XY. The bracket operation is boxdot(A)=Y*A*X^m-X^m*A*Y. The kernel R_{X^m} is freely generated by X,T_1 and boxdot of the permissible matching-bracket words T_1^{i_1} X^{j_1} ... X^{j_{k-1}} T_1^{i_k} of Lemma4.5, with i_a positive, 0<=j_a<m, and every right matching bracket preceded by T_1. The full source bracketing convention is retained. This does not assert a finite generating set, does not count the m=1 Weitzenboeck case separately, and does not broaden the explicit generator description to an arbitrary polynomial f.
original_metadata.source_boundary_note: The complete original Theorem 4.6 and full author proof are retained; the selected task is its homogeneous monomial branch m>=2. The bracket operator and all permissible-word conventions, full weighted kernel-spanning induction of Theorem 4.2/Corollary 4.3 and permissible-word construction of Lemma 4.5 are included as new core. The author uniquely recovers root and matching brackets from each leading monomial and rules out factorization by lower-weight permissible words. General locally nilpotent derivation classification, short equal-kernel rigidity and the known linear Weitzenboeck case are not counted.
